title: The joy of learning
hook: the Psalms call the Torah sweeter than honey (Psalm 19:11)
tomorrow: Noa's studied with Eli every night. does the Torah ever say stop?

segments.voice: Yesterday, Abraham bargaining, Habakkuk asking how long, Job arguing and praised. Doubt is allowed. Today, the other feeling that turns up in study, the one nobody warns you about.

A win small enough to fit in a text message. The chord you couldn't play, and then could. The recipe that finally tastes like your grandmother's. A line you've stumbled on all week, coming out whole. That rush has a flavor, and a Psalm names it. It says God's teachings are sweeter than honey. And an old custom took the Psalm at its word, and put real honey on the page.
screen: `A WIN THE SIZE OF A TEXT.` → `A LINE THAT COMES OUT WHOLE.` → `REAL HONEY ON THE PAGE.`

segments.voice: Psalm nineteen praises God's teaching, and then says of it, in the JPS translation: "More to be desired are they than gold, yea, than much fine gold; sweeter also than honey and the honeycomb." Gold is something you keep. Honey is something you taste, right now, on your tongue. The Psalm picks both. Tradition tells of a custom, kept in some communities, for a small child's first day of learning: the letters of the aleph-bet, written out and touched with honey, so the first taste of Torah would be sweet. The Talmud has its own picture. In the tractate Eruvin, the words of Torah are compared to a fig tree. Every time you search a fig tree, you find another fig. Every time you go back to a text, you find another taste. So joy isn't the reward you get after the hard part is over. It's part of the learning itself: the line that finally clicks, the question that opens instead of closing, the evening a cousin dances in the kitchen because he got a verse right. Something to tell a friend tonight: in some communities, a child's first lesson came with honey on the letters.
screen: `MORE THAN GOLD. SWEETER THAN HONEY.` · `HONEY ON THE ALEPH-BET.` · `A FIG TREE: ALWAYS ONE MORE.` · `JOY IS PART OF THE LEARNING.` · then, large: `SWEETER THAN HONEY.`

segments.voice: If you have something sweet nearby, a raisin, a spoon of honey, a piece of fruit, take one small taste. While it's still on your tongue, say one line you love, slowly, from these lessons or from anywhere. Let the two sit together until the sweetness fades.
screen: `ONE SMALL TASTE.` · `ONE LINE YOU LOVE.` · `LET THEM SIT TOGETHER.`

segments.voice: The joy of learning: the sweetness the Psalm finds in God's teaching, more than gold, more than honey. It belongs inside the study, not after it.
Your line: sweeter than honey. A fig tree always has one more fig. Talk tomorrow.

howItsDone: Some Jewish communities mark a young child's first day of Torah study with honey on the letters of the aleph-bet, and Psalm 19 is part of the Shabbat morning psalms in many prayer books.
